subject: math
title: Line Plots with Fractions: Halves, Fourths and Eighths
seo_title: Grade 4 Line Plots with Fractions Worksheets: Make and Read Line Plots in Eighths, Add and Subtract Measurements
standard_text: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8). Solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions by using information presented in line plots. For example, from a line plot find and interpret the difference in length between the longest and shortest specimens in an insect collection.
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 line plot worksheets with fractions: read and make line plots in halves, fourths and eighths, find the difference between the longest and shortest, add measurements and solve word problems. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: One X for each measurement. Subtract to compare, add to find a total.
key_sub: Mark the number line in eighths when the data has eighths, and put 2/8 above 1/4. The difference between the longest and shortest uses the X's farthest right and left, not the ends of the line.
body_html:
What a line plot shows

A line plot is a number line with an X for each measurement. When a length repeats, the X's stack up. The number line can be marked in halves, fourths or eighths of a unit.

On an eighths scale, the marks are 18, 14, 38, 12, 58, 34, 78, 1. Some marks are labeled in simplest form: 28 is written 14, 48 is 12 and 68 is 34.

Make a line plot

A class measured 10 beetles. The lengths in inches are: 48, 38, 1, 28, 78, 38, 12, 58, 38, 78.

Some lengths are eighths, so mark the number line in eighths. Then put one X above the mark for each length. 48 goes above 12, and 28 goes above 14.

Same lengthWhere it goes
28 = 14the mark labeled 14
48 = 12the mark labeled 12
68 = 34the mark labeled 34
88 = 1the mark labeled 1

Find a difference

To compare two lengths, subtract. To compare the longest and the shortest, use the X's farthest to the right and to the left.

Example

How much longer is the longest beetle than the shortest beetle?

Longest: 1 inch. Shortest: 14 inch. Write both in eighths: 1 = 88 and 14 = 28. 88 − 28 = 68.

Answer: 68 inch

Find a total

Each X is one measurement. To find the total length of the X's above one mark, add that length once for every X.

Example

The 3 beetles that are 38 inch long are put end to end. How long is the row?

38 + 38 + 38 = 98. 88 is 1 whole, so 98 = 1 18.

Answer: 1 18 inches

Example

What is the total length of the beetles that are 12 inch or 58 inch long?

2 X's above 12 and 1 X above 58. Write 12 as 48: 48 + 48 + 58 = 138 = 1 58.

Answer: 1 58 inches

On this page, answers keep the denominator of the problem: 48 is right, and so is 12.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading 38 as 34Look at the bottom number. Eighths are smaller pieces than fourths
Putting 28 at a new mark28 = 14, so it goes above 14
Using the ends of the number line as the longest and shortestUse the X's farthest to the right and left
Adding the denominators: 38 + 38 = 616The pieces stay eighths: 68
Adding 14 + 38 as 48Rename first: 28 + 38 = 58
Using the number of X's as the lengthEach X stands for one measurement. Add the lengths, not the X's

faq.q: What is a line plot with fractions in 4th grade?
faq.a: It is a number line marked in halves, fourths or eighths, with one X above the mark for each measurement. Students use it to find the most common length, the difference between lengths and the total of the measurements.

faq.q: How do you make a line plot with eighths?
faq.a: Draw a number line with a mark for every eighth from the smallest to the largest value, labeling marks like 2/8 as 1/4. Then put one X above the mark for each measurement.

faq.q: How do you find the difference between the longest and shortest on a line plot?
faq.a: Find the X farthest to the right and the X farthest to the left, then subtract. For 1 inch and 1/4 inch, write them as 8/8 and 2/8, so the difference is 6/8 inch.

faq.q: How do you find the total of the measurements at one mark?
faq.a: Add that length once for each X above it. Three X's above 3/8 inch give 3/8 + 3/8 + 3/8 = 9/8, which is 1 1/8 inches.

sets.title: Read a line plot with fractions

items.q: Ms. Lee's class measured some seed pods. The line plot shows the lengths. How many seed pods are 1 14 inches long?
items.e: Find 1 14 on the number line. Count only the X's in that column: 4. Do not count the X's above the marks next to it.

items.q: Sofia measured some acorns. The line plot shows the lengths. Which length is the most common?
items.e: The most common length has the tallest stack of X's. The stack above 1 58 has 4 X's, more than any other.

items.q: Mia measured some leaves. The line plot shows the lengths. How many leaves did Mia measure in all?
items.e: Each X is one leaf. Add the X's in every column: 2 + 3 + 2 + 3 + 1 = 11.

items.q: Mrs. Green's class measured some crickets. The line plot shows the lengths. How many crickets are 1 28 inches long?
items.e: The marks are labeled in simplest form. 1 28 = 1 14, so look at the mark labeled 1 14. Count the X's above it: 4.

items.q: Ms. Lee's class measured some feathers. The line plot shows the lengths. How long is the longest feather?
items.e: Look for the X that is farthest to the right: it is above 4. The mark 4 18 has no X, so no feather is that long.

items.q: Jack measured some caterpillars. The line plot shows the lengths. How many caterpillars are 1 34 inches long?
items.e: Find 1 34 on the number line. Count only the X's in that column: 2. Do not count the X's above the marks next to it.

items.q: Mr. Diaz's class measured some earthworms. The line plot shows the lengths. How many earthworms are longer than 4 14 inches?
items.e: Longer means to the right of 4 14. Do not count the X's above 4 14 itself. Add the X's to the right: 3 + 3 + 1 = 7.

items.q: Mrs. Green's class measured some ribbon pieces. The line plot shows the lengths. How long is the shortest ribbon piece?
items.e: Look for the X that is farthest to the left: it is above 2 14. The first mark, 2 18, has no X, so no ribbon piece is that short.

items.q: Leo measured some shells. The line plot shows the lengths. How many shells are 1 48 inches long?
items.e: The marks are labeled in simplest form. 1 48 = 1 12, so look at the mark labeled 1 12. Count the X's above it: 3.

items.q: Ms. Brown's class measured some pencils. The line plot shows the lengths. Which length is the most common?
items.e: The most common length has the tallest stack of X's. The stack above 4 14 has 5 X's, more than any other.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class measured some twigs. The line plot shows the lengths. How many twigs did the class measure in all?
items.e: Each X is one twig. Add the X's in every column: 1 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 10.

items.q: Ava measured some beetles. The line plot shows the lengths. How many beetles are 78 inch long?
items.e: Find 78 on the number line. Count only the X's in that column: 3. Do not count the X's above the marks next to it.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class measured some snail shells. The line plot shows the lengths. How many snail shells are longer than 1 inch?
items.e: Longer means to the right of 1. Do not count the X's above 1 itself. Add the X's to the right: 1 + 1 = 2.

items.e: Look for the X that is farthest to the right: it is above 1 34. The mark 2 has no X, so no paper clip is that long.

items.q: Ben measured some grasshoppers. The line plot shows the lengths. How many grasshoppers are 1 68 inches long?
items.e: The marks are labeled in simplest form. 1 68 = 1 34, so look at the mark labeled 1 34. Count the X's above it: 2.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class measured some crayons. The line plot shows the lengths. Which length is the most common?
items.e: The most common length has the tallest stack of X's. The stack above 3 38 has 4 X's, more than any other.

items.q: Kai measured some pine cones. The line plot shows the lengths. How long is the shortest pine cone?
items.e: Look for the X that is farthest to the left: it is above 3 34. The first mark, 3 12, has no X, so no pine cone is that short.

items.q: Ruby measured some seed pods. The line plot shows the lengths. How many seed pods are 2 12 inches long?

sets.title: Make a line plot from data

items.q: Sam measured 10 crickets. The lengths in inches are: 1 58, 1 12, 1 12, 1 12, 1 38, 1, 1 38, 1 58, 1 58, 1 18. He made this line plot but forgot one X. Where does the missing X go?
items.e: Count how many times each length is in the list. 1 38 is in the list 2 times, but the plot shows only 1 X above it. The missing X goes above 1 38.

items.q: Owen measured 9 feathers. The lengths in inches are: 4 14, 4 18, 4 12, 4 18, 3 78, 4 18, 4 38, 4 38, 4. He made this line plot but forgot one X. Where does the missing X go?
items.e: Count how many times each length is in the list. 4 38 is in the list 2 times, but the plot shows only 1 X above it. The missing X goes above 4 38.

items.q: Lily measured 9 caterpillars. The lengths in inches are: 1 34, 2, 1 12, 1 14, 2 14, 1 12, 1 14, 1 12, 1 34. She made this line plot but forgot one X. Where does the missing X go?
items.e: Count how many times each length is in the list. 1 12 is in the list 3 times, but the plot shows only 2 X's above it. The missing X goes above 1 12.

items.q: Maya measured 10 earthworms. The lengths in inches are: 5, 4 78, 5, 4 78, 4 58, 4 34, 4 78, 4 78, 4 38, 4 78. She made this line plot but forgot one X. Where does the missing X go?
items.e: Count how many times each length is in the list. 5 is in the list 2 times, but the plot shows only 1 X above it. The missing X goes above 5.

items.q: Eli measured 10 ribbon pieces. The lengths in inches are: 2 14, 2 14, 2 18, 2, 2 58, 2, 2 38, 2 12, 2 12, 2 18. He made this line plot but forgot one X. Where does the missing X go?
items.e: Count how many times each length is in the list. 2 58 is in the list once, but the plot has no X above it. The missing X goes above 2 58.

items.q: Ms. Lee's class measured 9 pencils. The lengths in inches are: 5 68, 5 12, 5 38, 5 34, 5 78, 5 58, 5 58, 5 12, 5 12. The class makes a line plot marked in eighths, with each mark labeled in simplest form. How many X's go above 5 34?
items.e: 5 68 = 5 34, so both go above the same mark. In the list, 5 34 appears once and 5 68 appears once: 1 + 1 = 2 X's.

items.q: Mr. Diaz's class measured 10 beetles. The lengths in inches are: 1 58, 1 78, 1 58, 1 48, 1 12, 1 58, 2, 1 48, 1 12, 1 58. The class makes a line plot marked in eighths, with each mark labeled in simplest form. How many X's go above 1 12?
items.e: 1 48 = 1 12, so both go above the same mark. In the list, 1 12 appears 2 times and 1 48 appears 2 times: 2 + 2 = 4 X's.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class measured 8 snail shells. The lengths in inches are: 1 28, 1 18, 1 58, 1 14, 1 18, 1 18, 1 14, 1 38. The class makes a line plot marked in eighths, with each mark labeled in simplest form. How many X's go above 1 14?
items.e: 1 28 = 1 14, so both go above the same mark. In the list, 1 14 appears 2 times and 1 28 appears once: 2 + 1 = 3 X's.

items.q: Ms. Brown's class measured 8 paper clips. The lengths in inches are: 1 28, 1 38, 1 34, 1 34, 1 38, 1 14, 1 14, 1 14. The class makes a line plot marked in eighths, with each mark labeled in simplest form. How many X's go above 1 14?
items.e: 1 28 = 1 14, so both go above the same mark. In the list, 1 14 appears 3 times and 1 28 appears once: 3 + 1 = 4 X's.

items.q: Luis measured 7 crickets. The lengths in inches are: 1 14, 1 12, 1 18, 1 34, 1 38, 1 12, 1 58. Which scale should the line plot use so every length has a mark?
items.e: Some lengths, like 1 18 and 1 58, are eighths of an inch. Halves and fourths have no mark for them, so the number line must be marked in eighths.

items.q: Noah measured 6 acorns: 1 12, 1 34, 2 14, 2, 2 12, 1 78 inches. He makes a line plot marked in fourths: 1 12, 1 34, 2, 2 14, 2 12. Which length has no mark on this line plot?
items.e: A fourths scale only has marks at 0, 14, 12, 34, 1 and so on. 1 78 is an eighth, so it falls between two marks. The line plot needs to be marked in eighths.

items.q: Zoe measured 6 snail shells: 34, 12, 1 14, 1, 38, 34 inches. She makes a line plot marked in fourths: 14, 12, 34, 1, 1 14. Which length has no mark on this line plot?
items.e: A fourths scale only has marks at 0, 14, 12, 34, 1 and so on. 38 is an eighth, so it falls between two marks. The line plot needs to be marked in eighths.

items.q: Mr. Kim's class measured some grasshoppers. The line plot shows the lengths. Which list of lengths (in inches) matches the line plot?

1, 1 38, 1 12, 1 12, 1 12, 1 34
1, 1 38, 1 38, 1 12, 1 12, 1 12
1, 1 38, 1 12, 1 12, 1 12, 1 12
items.e: Read each X: 1 X above 1, 2 X's above 1 38, 3 X's above 1 12. That is 6 lengths, the same as the 6 X's on the plot.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class measured some crayons. The line plot shows the lengths. Which list of lengths (in inches) matches the line plot?
c: 3 12, 3 34, 3 34, 3 34, 3 34

2 34, 3 12, 3 34, 3 34, 3 34, 3 34

items.e: Read each X: 1 X above 2 34, 1 X above 3 12, 4 X's above 3 34. That is 6 lengths, the same as the 6 X's on the plot.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class measured some pine cones. The line plot shows the lengths. Which list of lengths (in inches) matches the line plot?
c: 2 58, 2 58, 2 34, 2 34, 2 34, 3 14
2 58, 2 58, 2 34, 2 34, 2 34, 3 18
2 58, 2 34, 2 34, 2 34, 3 18

items.e: Read each X: 2 X's above 2 58, 3 X's above 2 34, 1 X above 3 18. That is 6 lengths, the same as the 6 X's on the plot.

items.q: Grace measured some seed pods. The line plot shows the lengths. Which list of lengths (in inches) matches the line plot?
c: 1 18, 1 12, 1 58, 1 58, 1 58
1 14, 1 12, 1 58, 1 58, 1 58
1 18, 1 58, 1 58, 1 58, 1 58
1 18, 1 12, 1 58, 1 58
items.e: Read each X: 1 X above 1 18, 1 X above 1 12, 3 X's above 1 58. That is 5 lengths, the same as the 5 X's on the plot.

items.q: Emma made this line plot of acorn lengths. Then she measured one more acorn. It is 1 28 inches long. Above which mark should she draw the X?
items.e: 1 28 = 1 14 (divide the top and bottom by 2). The mark is labeled 1 14, so the X goes there.

items.q: Sofia made this line plot of leaf lengths. Then she measured one more leaf. It is 2 68 inches long. Above which mark should she draw the X?
items.e: 2 68 = 2 34 (divide the top and bottom by 2). The mark is labeled 2 34, so the X goes there.

items.q: Mia made this line plot of cricket lengths. Then she measured one more cricket. It is 128 inches long. Above which mark should she draw the X?
items.e: 128 is more than 1: 128 = 88 + 48 = 1 48 = 1 12. The X goes above 1 12.

items.q: Jack made this line plot of caterpillar lengths. Then he measured one more caterpillar. It is 98 inches long. Above which mark should he draw the X?
items.e: 98 is more than 1: 98 = 88 + 18 = 1 18. The X goes above 1 18.

sets.title: Difference between the longest and shortest

items.q: Mr. Kim's class measured some earthworms. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest earthworm than the shortest earthworm?
items.e: Longest: 3 18 inches. Shortest: 2 12 inches. Write them in eighths: 2 12 = 2 48. Subtract: 3 18 − 2 48. 18 is less than 48, so rename 1 whole as 88: 3 18 = 2 98. Subtract the fractions: 98 − 48 = 58. Subtract the whole numbers: 2 − 2 = 0. The answer is 58 inch.

items.q: Ms. Brown's class measured some ribbon pieces. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest ribbon piece than the shortest ribbon piece?
items.e: Longest: 4 38 inches. Shortest: 3 34 inches. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line. Write them in eighths: 3 34 = 3 68. Subtract: 4 38 − 3 68. 38 is less than 68, so rename 1 whole as 88: 4 38 = 3 118. Subtract the fractions: 118 − 68 = 58. Subtract the whole numbers: 3 − 3 = 0. The answer is 58 inch.

items.q: Leo measured some beetles. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest beetle than the shortest beetle?
items.e: Longest: 2 12 inches. Shortest: 1 14 inches. Write them in fourths: 2 12 = 2 24. Subtract: 2 24 − 1 14. Subtract the fractions: 24 − 14 = 14. Subtract the whole numbers: 2 − 1 = 1. The answer is 1 14 inches.

items.q: Ms. Lee's class measured some snail shells. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest snail shell than the shortest snail shell?
items.e: Longest: 1 38 inches. Shortest: 58 inch. Subtract: 1 38 − 58. 38 is less than 58, so rename 1 whole as 88: 1 38 = 118. Subtract the fractions: 118 − 58 = 68. The answer is 68 inch.

items.q: Mr. Kim's class measured some paper clips. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest paper clip than the shortest paper clip?
items.e: Longest: 1 34 inches. Shortest: 1 18 inches. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line. Write them in eighths: 1 34 = 1 68. Subtract: 1 68 − 1 18. Subtract the fractions: 68 − 18 = 58. Subtract the whole numbers: 1 − 1 = 0. The answer is 58 inch.

items.q: Ava measured some crayons. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest crayon than the shortest crayon?
items.e: Longest: 3 12 inches. Shortest: 2 34 inches. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line. Write them in fourths: 3 12 = 3 24. Subtract: 3 24 − 2 34. 24 is less than 34, so rename 1 whole as 44: 3 24 = 2 64. Subtract the fractions: 64 − 34 = 34. Subtract the whole numbers: 2 − 2 = 0. The answer is 34 inch.

items.q: Nora measured some pine cones. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest pine cone than the shortest pine cone?
items.e: Longest: 3 inches. Shortest: 2 14 inches. Write them in eighths: 2 14 = 2 28. Subtract: 3 − 2 28. There is no fraction to take 28 from, so rename 1 whole: 3 = 2 88. Subtract the fractions: 88 − 28 = 68. Subtract the whole numbers: 2 − 2 = 0. The answer is 68 inch.

items.q: Ben measured some seed pods. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest seed pod than the shortest seed pod?
items.e: Longest: 2 34 inches. Shortest: 2 inches. Use the X's, not the ends of the number line. Write them in eighths: 2 34 = 2 68. Subtract: 2 68 − 2. Subtract the whole numbers: 2 − 2 = 0. The answer is 68 inch.

items.q: Kai measured some leaves. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest leaf than the shortest leaf?
items.e: Longest: 4 14 inches. Shortest: 2 34 inches. Subtract: 4 14 − 2 34. 14 is less than 34, so rename 1 whole as 44: 4 14 = 3 54. Subtract the fractions: 54 − 34 = 24. Subtract the whole numbers: 3 − 2 = 1. The answer is 1 24 inches.

items.q: Ruby measured some crickets. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the longest cricket than the shortest cricket?
items.e: Longest: 2 inches. Shortest: 1 18 inches. Subtract: 2 − 1 18. There is no fraction to take 18 from, so rename 1 whole: 2 = 1 88. Subtract the fractions: 88 − 18 = 78. Subtract the whole numbers: 1 − 1 = 0. The answer is 78 inch.

items.q: Omar measured some feathers. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the most common length than the shortest length?
items.e: Most common: 5 12 inches (the tallest stack). Shortest: 4 78 inches. Write them in eighths: 5 12 = 5 48. Subtract: 5 48 − 4 78. 48 is less than 78, so rename 1 whole as 88: 5 48 = 4 128. Subtract the fractions: 128 − 78 = 58. Subtract the whole numbers: 4 − 4 = 0. The answer is 58 inch.

items.q: Mr. Diaz's class measured some ants. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the most common length than the shortest length?
items.e: Most common: 38 inch (the tallest stack). Shortest: 18 inch. Subtract: 38 − 18. Subtract the numerators: 3 − 1 = 2. Keep the denominator 8: 28 inch.

items.q: Sam measured some caterpillars. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the most common length than the shortest length?
items.e: Most common: 1 12 inches (the tallest stack). Shortest: 1 inch. Write them in fourths: 1 12 = 1 24. Subtract: 1 24 − 1. Subtract the whole numbers: 1 − 1 = 0. The answer is 24 inch.

items.q: Mr. Kim's class measured some earthworms. The line plot shows the lengths. How much longer is the most common length than the shortest length?
items.e: Most common: 3 34 inches (the tallest stack). Shortest: 3 38 inches. Write them in eighths: 3 34 = 3 68. Subtract: 3 68 − 3 38. Subtract the fractions: 68 − 38 = 38. Subtract the whole numbers: 3 − 3 = 0. The answer is 38 inch.

items.q: Owen measured 5 bean sprouts. The lengths in inches are: 68, 38, 78, 12, 14. What is the difference between the longest and the shortest?
items.e: Find the longest, 78 inch, and the shortest, 14 inch. Do not just use the first and last numbers in the list. Write them in eighths: 14 = 28. Subtract: 78 − 28. Subtract the numerators: 7 − 2 = 5. Keep the denominator 8: 58 inch.

items.q: Lily measured 6 crayons. The lengths in inches are: 3 14, 3 58, 3, 3 78, 3 12, 3 38. What is the difference between the longest and the shortest?
items.e: Find the longest, 3 78 inches, and the shortest, 3 inches. Do not just use the first and last numbers in the list. Subtract: 3 78 − 3. Subtract the whole numbers: 3 − 3 = 0. The answer is 78 inch.

items.q: Maya measured 5 seed pods. The lengths in inches are: 1 34, 1 18, 2 48, 1 12, 2 18. What is the difference between the longest and the shortest?
items.e: Find the longest, 2 12 inches, and the shortest, 1 18 inches. Do not just use the first and last numbers in the list. Write them in eighths: 2 12 = 2 48. Subtract: 2 48 − 1 18. Subtract the fractions: 48 − 18 = 38. Subtract the whole numbers: 2 − 1 = 1. The answer is 1 38 inches.

items.q: Eli measured 6 leaves. The lengths in inches are: 2 34, 3 48, 2 38, 3 18, 3 34, 2 12. What is the difference between the longest and the shortest?
items.e: Find the longest, 3 34 inches, and the shortest, 2 38 inches. Do not just use the first and last numbers in the list. Write them in eighths: 3 34 = 3 68. Subtract: 3 68 − 2 38. Subtract the fractions: 68 − 38 = 38. Subtract the whole numbers: 3 − 2 = 1. The answer is 1 38 inches.

items.q: Luis's longest feather is 78 inch longer than his shortest feather. The shortest feather is 2 58 inches long. How long is the longest feather?
items.e: Longer means add: 2 58 + 78. Add the fractions: 58 + 78 = 128 = 1 12. So 2 + 1 12 = 3 12 inches.

items.q: Noah's longest twig is 58 inch longer than his shortest twig. The shortest twig is 4 14 inches long. How long is the longest twig?
items.e: Longer means add: 4 14 + 58. Add the fractions: 28 + 58 = 78. So the longest is 4 78 inches.

sets.title: Add measurements from a line plot

items.q: Zoe measured some ribbon pieces. The line plot shows the lengths. The ribbon pieces that are 4 12 inches long are put end to end. What is their total length?
items.e: There are 3 X's above 4 12, so add 4 12 3 times. Add the fractions: 12 + 12 + 12 = 32. Add the whole numbers: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12. 32 = 1 12, so 12 + 1 12 = 13 12 inches.

items.q: Mrs. Green's class measured some shells. The line plot shows the lengths. The shells that are 2 18 inches long are put end to end. What is their total length?
items.e: There are 4 X's above 2 18, so add 2 18 4 times. Add the fractions: 18 + 18 + 18 + 18 = 48. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 2 + 2 + 2 = 8. Put them together: 8 48 inches.

items.q: Mr. Diaz's class measured some pencils. The line plot shows the lengths. The pencils that are 6 14 inches long are put end to end. What is their total length?
items.e: There are 2 X's above 6 14, so add 6 14 2 times. Add the fractions: 14 + 14 = 24. Add the whole numbers: 6 + 6 = 12. Put them together: 12 24 inches.

items.q: Grace measured some twigs. The line plot shows the lengths. The twigs that are 4 14 inches long are put end to end. What is their total length?
items.e: There are 2 X's above 4 14, so add 4 14 2 times. Add the fractions: 14 + 14 = 24. Add the whole numbers: 4 + 4 = 8. Put them together: 8 24 inches.

items.q: Emma measured some beetles. The line plot shows the lengths. The beetles that are 1 12 inches long are put end to end. What is their total length?
items.e: There are 4 X's above 1 12, so add 1 12 4 times. Add the fractions: 12 + 12 + 12 + 12 = 42. Add the whole numbers: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4. 42 = 2, so 4 + 2 = 6 inches.

items.q: Sofia measured some snail shells. The line plot shows the lengths. The snail shells that are 1 18 inches long are put end to end. What is their total length?
items.e: There are 4 X's above 1 18, so add 1 18 4 times. Add the fractions: 18 + 18 + 18 + 18 = 48. Add the whole numbers: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4. Put them together: 4 48 inches.

items.q: Mr. Kim's class measured some grasshoppers. The line plot shows the lengths. The grasshoppers that are 2 14 inches long are put end to end. What is their total length?
items.e: There are 2 X's above 2 14, so add 2 14 2 times. Add the fractions: 14 + 14 = 24. Add the whole numbers: 2 + 2 = 4. Put them together: 4 24 inches.

items.q: Mia measured some crayons. The line plot shows the lengths. The crayons that are 3 38 inches long are put end to end. What is their total length?
items.e: There are 3 X's above 3 38, so add 3 38 3 times. Add the fractions: 38 + 38 + 38 = 98. Add the whole numbers: 3 + 3 + 3 = 9. 98 = 1 18, so 9 + 1 18 = 10 18 inches.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class measured some leaves. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of all the leaves that are 3 18 inches or 3 14 inches long?
items.e: The plot has 3 X's above 3 18 and 2 X's above 3 14. Write them in eighths: 3 14 = 3 28. Add the fractions: 18 + 18 + 18 + 28 + 28 = 78. Add the whole numbers: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 15. Put them together: 15 78 inches.

items.q: Mrs. Patel's class measured some feathers. The line plot shows the lengths. What is the total length of all the feathers that are 3 12 inches or 3 78 inches long?
items.e: The plot has 2 X's above 3 12 and 2 X's above 3 78. Write them in eighths: 3 12 = 3 48. Add the fractions: 48 + 48 + 78 + 78 = 228. Add the whole numbers: 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 12. 228 = 2 68, so 12 + 2 68 = 14 68 inches.
